verses.zh: （扫罗打发人窥探大卫的房屋，要杀他。那时，大卫作这金诗，交与伶长。调用休要毁坏。）我的　神啊，求你救我脱离仇敌，把我安置在高处，得脱那些起来攻击我的人。
verses.en: For the music director, according to the al-tashcheth style;[NOTE:1] a prayer[NOTE:2] of David, written when Saul sent men to surround his house and murder him.[NOTE:3] Deliver me from my enemies, my God.Protect me[NOTE:4] from those who attack me.[NOTE:5]
notes: Psalm 59. The psalmist calls down judgment on his foreign enemies, whom he compares to ravenous wild dogs.
Heb “do not destroy.” Perhaps this refers to a particular style of music, a tune title, or a musical instrument. These words also appear in the superscription to Pss 57-58, 75.
The precise meaning of the Hebrew word מִכְתָּם (miktam), which also appears in the heading to Pss 16, 56-58, 60 is uncertain. HALOT 582-83 s.v. defines it as “inscription.”

Heb “when Saul sent and they watched his house in order to kill him.”sn According to the superscription, David wrote this psalm on the occasion when Saul sent assassins to surround David’s house and kill him in the morning (see 1 Sam 19:11). However, the psalm itself mentions foreign enemies (vv. 5, 8). Perhaps these references reflect a later adaptation of an original Davidic psalm.
Or “make me secure”; Heb “set me on high.”

verses.zh: 求你救我脱离作孽的人和喜爱流人血的人！
verses.en: Deliver me from evildoers.[NOTE:1] Rescue me from violent men.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “from those who raise themselves up [against] me.”
Heb “from the workers of wickedness.”

verses.zh: 因为，他们埋伏要害我的命；有能力的人聚集来攻击我。耶和华啊，这不是为我的过犯，也不是为我的罪愆。
verses.en: For look, they wait to ambush me;[NOTE:1] powerful men stalk[NOTE:2] me,but not because I have rebelled or sinned, O Lord.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “from men of bloodshed.”
Heb “my life.”
The Hebrew verb is from the root גּוּר (gur), which means “to challenge, attack” in Isa 54:15 and “to stalk” (with hostile intent) in Ps 56:8.

verses.zh: 我虽然无过，他们预备整齐，跑来攻击我。求你兴起鉴察，帮助我！
verses.en: Though I have done nothing wrong,[NOTE:1] they are anxious to attack.[NOTE:2] Spring into action and help me. Take notice of me.[NOTE:3]
notes: The point is that the psalmist’s enemies have no justifiable reason for attacking him. He has neither rebelled or sinned against the Lord.
Heb “without sin.”
Heb “they run and they are determined.”

verses.zh: 万军之　神―耶和华以色列的　神啊！求你兴起，惩治万邦！不要怜悯行诡诈的恶人！（细拉）
verses.en: You, O Lord God of Heaven’s Armies,[NOTE:1] the God of Israel,rouse yourself and punish[NOTE:2] all the nations.Have no mercy on any treacherous evildoers. (Selah)
notes: Heb “arise to meet me and see.” The Hebrew verb קָרָא (qaraʾ, “to meet; to encounter”) here carries the nuance of “to help.”

Heb “Lord, God, Hosts.” One expects the construct form אֱלֹהֵי (ʾelohe) before צְבָאוֹת (tsevaʾot, “hosts”). See Ps 89:9, but יְהוָה אֱלֹהִים (yehvah ʾelohim) precedes צְבָאוֹת (tsevaʾot) in Pss 80:4, 19; 84:8 as well.

verses.zh: 他们晚上转回，叫号如狗，围城绕行。
verses.en: They return in the evening;they growl[NOTE:1] like dogsand prowl around outside[NOTE:2] the city.
notes: Heb “wake up to punish” (see Pss 35:23; 44:23).
Or “howl”; or “bark.”

verses.zh: 他们口中喷吐恶言，嘴里有刀；他们说：有谁听见？
verses.en: Look, they hurl insults at meand openly threaten to kill me,[NOTE:1] for they say,[NOTE:2] “Who hears?”
notes: Heb “go around.”
Heb “look, they gush forth with their mouth, swords [are] in their lips.”

verses.zh: 但你―耶和华必笑话他们；你要嗤笑万邦。
verses.en: But you, O Lord, laugh in disgust at them;[NOTE:1] you taunt[NOTE:2] all the nations.
notes: The words “for they say” are supplied in the translation for clarification. The following question (“Who hears?”) is spoken by the psalmist’s enemies, who are confident that no one else can hear their threats against the psalmist. They are aggressive because they feel the psalmist is vulnerable and has no one to help him.
Laugh in disgust. See Pss 2:4; 37:13.

verses.zh: 我的力量啊，我必仰望你，因为　神是我的高台。
verses.en: You are my source of strength. I will wait for you.[NOTE:1] For God is my refuge.[NOTE:2]
notes: Or “scoff at”; or “deride”; or “mock” (see Ps 2:4).

Heb “his strength, for you I will watch.” “His strength” should be emended to “my strength” (see v. 17). Some also emend אֶשְׁמֹרָה (ʾeshmorah, “I will watch”) to אֱזַמֵּרָה (ʾezammerah, “I will sing praises [to you]”) See v. 17.

verses.zh: 我的　神要以慈爱迎接我；　神要叫我看见我仇敌遭报。
verses.en: The God who loves me will help me;[NOTE:1] God will enable me to triumph over[NOTE:2] my enemies.[NOTE:3]
notes: Or “my elevated place” (see Ps 18:2).
Heb “the God of my [Qere (marginal reading); the Kethib (consonantal text) has “his”] loyal love will meet me.”
Heb “will cause me to look upon.”

verses.zh: 不要杀他们，恐怕我的民忘记。主啊，你是我们的盾牌；求你用你的能力使他们四散，且降为卑。
verses.en: Do not strike them dead suddenly,because then my people might forget the lesson.[NOTE:1] Use your power to make them homeless vagabonds and then bring them down,O Lord who shields us.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “those who watch me [with evil intent].” See also Pss 5:8; 27:11; 54:5; 56:2.

My people might forget the lesson. Swift, sudden destruction might be quickly forgotten. The psalmist wants God’s judgment to be prolonged so that it might be a continual reminder of divine justice.tn Heb “do not kill them, lest my people forget.”

verses.zh: 因他们口中的罪和嘴里的言语，并咒骂虚谎的话，愿他们在骄傲之中被缠住了。
verses.en: They speak sinful words.[NOTE:1] So let them be trapped by their own prideand by the curses and lies they speak.
notes: Heb “make them roam around by your strength and bring them down, O our shield, the Lord.”

verses.zh: 求你发怒，使他们消灭，以致归于无有，叫他们知道　神在雅各中间掌权，直到地极。（细拉）
verses.en: Angrily wipe them out. Wipe them out so they vanish.Let them know that God rulesover Jacob and to the ends of the earth. (Selah)

verses.zh: 到了晚上，任凭他们转回；任凭他们叫号如狗，围城绕行。
verses.en: They return in the evening;they growl[NOTE:1] like dogsand prowl around outside[NOTE:2] the city.
notes: Heb “the sin of their mouth [is] the word of their lips.”
Or “howl”; or “bark.”

verses.zh: 他们必走来走去，寻找食物，若不得饱就终夜在外。
verses.en: They wander around looking for something to eat;they refuse to sleep until they are full.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “go around.”

verses.zh: 但我要歌颂你的力量，早晨要高唱你的慈爱；因为你作过我的高台，在我急难的日子作过我的避难所。
verses.en: As for me, I will sing about your strength;I will praise your loyal love in the morning.For you are my refuge[NOTE:1] and my place of shelter when I face trouble.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “if they are not full, they stay through the night.”
Or “my elevated place” (see Ps 18:2).

verses.zh: 我的力量啊，我要歌颂你；因为　神是我的高台，是赐恩与我的　神。
verses.en: You are my source of strength. I will sing praises to you.[NOTE:1] For God is my refuge,[NOTE:2] the God who loves me.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “and my shelter in the day of my distress.”
Heb “my strength, to you I will sing praises.”
Or “my elevated place” (see Ps 18:2).
